Hi Samir — following the call, a concise technical summary:

Observed symptoms (Nov 2/4/5):
- Short-lived tail-latency spikes coincident with large, concurrent batched scoring jobs.
- KV cache pressure on the shared routing group causing cache evictions and a burst of recompute across replicas.
- A small fraction of requests experienced 3x token compute time for the first 2–4 tokens.

Immediate mitigations applied (Nov 6):
- Isolated your scoring route into a soft partition so it no longer shares KV cache with bursty feeding jobs.
- Adjusted batching window thresholds for your route to prefer lower-latency batching during critical windows.

Proposed durable changes:
1) Dedicated inference pool for the route (recommended) — eliminates noisy-neighbor cache impact and gives predictable tail-latency.
2) Optional quantized model variant for non-critical batch scoring to reduce compute time and cost.
3) Add a tracing hook for token-level latency alerts tied to your PagerDuty trigger.

Commercial tie-ins we can offer: 30-day trial of a 2-GPU dedicated pool at 50% list for validation; if validated within the trial, apply a 3% per-month commit discount for the first year of any committed capacity expansion. Also propose the 10% one-off credit Marissa suggested for November.

I've attached a short diagnostics export and the raw traces for the Nov 5 window.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
